questions.title: GATE CSE 2007 | Question: 27
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the set of (column) vectors defined by$$X = \left \{x \in R^3 \mid x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = 0, \text{ where } x^T = \left[x_1,x_2,x_3\right]^T\right \}$$.Which of the following is TRUE?

  1. $\left\{\left[1,-1,0\right]^T,\left[1,0,-1\right]^T\right\}$ is a basis for the subspace $X$.
  2. $\left\{\left[1,-1,0\right]^T,\left[1,0,-1\right]^T\right\}$ is a linearly independent set, but it does not span $X$ and therefore is not a basis of $X$.
  3. $X$ is not a subspace of $R^3$.
  4. None of the above

questions.title: GATE IT 2007 | Question: 52
questions.subject: Unknown
questions.questionHtml:
Given the following algorithm for sorting an array X and N numbers:

 SUBROUTINE SHORT (X, N)
                                IF (N < 2)
                                          RETURN
                                FOR (i = 2) TO N INCREMENT BY 1)
                                FOR (j = 1) TO i INCREMENT BY 1)
                                IF (X [i] > X [j])
                                          CONTINUE
                                TEMP = X[i]
                                X[i] = X[j]
                                X[j] = TEMP
                  END FOR
END SUBROUTINE

A good approximation of Halstead's estimated program length is

  1. 20
  2. 50
  3. 80
  4. 110

questions.title: GATE IT 2007 | Question: 57
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
In a multi-user operating system on an average, $20$ requests are made to use a particular resource per hour. The arrival of requests follows a Poisson distribution. The probability that either one, three or five requests are made in $45$ minutes is given by :

  1. $6.9 \times 10^6 \times e^{-20}$
  2. $1.02 \times 10^6 \times e^{-20}$
  3. $6.9 \times 10^3 \times e^{-20}$
  4. $1.02 \times 10^3 \times e^{-20}$

questions.title: GATE IT 2007 | Question: 76
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the sequence $\langle x_n \rangle , \: n \geq 0$ defined by the recurrence relation $x_{n+1} = c . x^2_n -2$, where $c > 0$.

Suppose there exists a non-empty, open interval $(a, b)$ such that for all $x_0$ satisfying $a < x_0 < b$, the sequence converges to a limit. The sequence converges to the value?

  1. $\frac{1+\sqrt{1+8c}}{2c}$
  2. $\frac{1-\sqrt{1+8c}}{2c}$
  3. $2$
  4. $\frac{2}{2c-1}$
